blocks.text: The OCA describes a mid-eighteenth-century image given to the Lavra in 1852 and placed in the cave church of Saint Michael. Its account identifies Thekla Adrianova’s reported 1869 healing and the subsequent blessing of Saint Innocent of Moscow. These details concern the shrine’s history and published miracle tradition, not the creation date of the selected 1877 copy.

blocks.text: The source says the original celebration followed Ilyin-Chernigov’s April 16 feast and was later moved to September 1, the reported day of glorification. Its account emphasizes the spiritual links among the Lavra, the caves, and the earlier Chernigov image.

blocks.text:
And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.

And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
blocks.context: Related Gospel narrative of Mary and Christ; not the icon’s later origin story.
